subcommittees.name: Public Lands, Forests, and Mining Subcommittee

dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts geothermal operators and property owners conducting exploration on non-federal surface estates meeting ownership criteria.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall not require an operator to obtain a Federal drilling permit for geothermal exploration

dimensions.assessment: Eliminates federal permit requirements and environmental review hurdles for qualifying geothermal developers.
dimensions.evidence: shall not be considered a major Federal action for the purposes of section 102(2)(C) of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969

dimensions.assessment: Does not alter royalty obligations due to the United States, maintaining baseline revenue structures.
dimensions.evidence: Nothing in this section shall affect the amount of royalties due to the United States under this Act

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Geothermal Steam Act of 1970 to carve out specific exemptions from multiple federal environmental statutes.
dimensions.evidence: The Geothermal Steam Act of 1970... is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Provides a permanent statutory exemption under the Geothermal Steam Act for qualifying operations.
dimensions.evidence: The Geothermal Steam Act of 1970 (30 U.S.C. 1001 et seq.) is amended

missing_information: The exact number of projects or total acreage expected to qualify for the exemption is not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: Exempts certain geothermal activities on state and private lands from federal drilling permits, NEPA reviews, and certain environmental consultations under specific ownership conditions.

related.label: H.Res. 1189
related.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 4690) to amend the Energy Conservation and Production Act to repeal certain Federal building energy efficiency performance standards, and for other purposes; providing for consideration of the resolution (H. Res. 1182) expressing support for rural communities across the United States as stewards of the environment, major suppliers of United States energy resources, critical providers of food production and manufacturing capacity, and drivers of national economic stability, and recognizing the work of the House of Representatives in the 119th Congress in support of those vital communities; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1897) to amend the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to optimize conservation through resource prioritization, incentivize wildlife conservation on private lands, provide for greater incentives to recover listed species, create greater transparency and accountability in recovering listed species, streamline the permitting process, eliminate barriers to conservation, and restore congressional intent; and providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 5587) to amend the Geothermal Steam Act of 1970 to waive the requirement for a Federal drilling permit for certain activities, to exempt certain activities from the requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, and for other purposes.
